title: The trypanosome undulating membrane is a liquid film drawn up along a flagellum

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The trypanosome undulating membrane is a liquid film drawn up along a flagellum

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The undulating membrane of trypanosomes and related flagellates forms when the flagellum lies near and parallel to the body and the fluid surface protoplasm is drawn up as a film along it, as a soap-film would be; the membrane is thus a liquid film of constant mean curvature whose undulations are produced by molecular tensions, not by its own active mobility.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It is a plausible assumption to suppose that, as the flagellum waves about, it comes to lie near and parallel to the body of the cell, and that the frill or undulating membrane is formed by the clear, fluid protoplasm of the surface layer springing up in a film to run up and along the flagellum, just as a soap-film would be formed in similar circumstances.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Undulating membranes of flagellates”. Scope: trypanosomes, Trichomonas and related flagellates, and spermatozoa with undulating membranes

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-23: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.61

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The passive-film model makes clear structural and dynamical predictions that can be compared with active alternatives. Open microscopy resolves major parts of the claim, but comprehensive curvature and force measurements across all named groups are unavailable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use ultrastructure and live imaging to test whether the membrane is a fluid film of constant mean curvature lacking active machinery, versus a structurally integrated, actively driven flagellum-attached membrane.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Constant curvature alone would not uniquely identify a passive liquid film.

Few datasets combine ultrastructure, curvature, and dynamics.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Open trypanosome tomograms can decide whether the membrane along the flagellum is an empty film or a fold built on an axoneme. That resolves the structural core for Trypanosoma brucei and leaves the developmental story, the constancy of mean curvature, and the denial of active motility only partly tested. Related flagellates in the stated scope are not in the same deposits.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Segment the trypanosome undulating membrane in three-dimensional electron microscopy and test whether its surface has constant mean curvature and lacks internal cytoplasm and cytoskeleton. A naked film whose waves persist without flagellar bending would support the claim; a cytoplasmic fold waved by the flagellar apparatus would refute the soap-film account.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Available tomograms center on the axoneme and paraflagellar rod, so the mean curvature of the whole undulating membrane is only partly in frame.

Trichomonas and spermatozoa with undulating membranes are outside this trypanosome archive, and static maps do not show whether the wave is actively driven.
